name: ChatGPT
bestFor: All-round everyday use, voice, images and plugins in one app
summary: The broadest general-purpose AI assistant: chat, web search, image generation, voice mode, file analysis and agents in one subscription.
does: Answers, writes, searches the web, makes images and runs agent tasks in one chat
strengths: Widest feature set in one subscription
Image generation built into the chat
watchOut: Writing drifts toward a recognisable house style
Plan and model names change often

name: Claude
bestFor: Long-form writing, careful reasoning and coding
summary: An assistant known for natural writing, long-document analysis and strong coding, with Projects, Artifacts and Claude Code included in paid plans.
does: Reads long material, writes in a natural voice and works through code
strengths: Claude Code included in paid plans
watchOut: Pro plan limits are shared with Claude Code

name: Gemini
bestFor: People who live in Gmail, Docs and Android
summary: Google's assistant, built into Workspace and Android, with Google Search grounding and cloud storage bundled into its paid plans.
does: Answers with Google Search grounding and works inside Google Workspace
strengths: Built into Gmail, Docs, Sheets and Drive
Paid plan bundles Google One storage

name: GitHub Copilot
bestFor: Teams already on GitHub who want low-friction completions in any IDE
summary: The most widely deployed coding assistant: inline completions, chat and a coding agent across VS Code, JetBrains, Visual Studio and GitHub itself.
does: Completes code as you type, answers questions and opens pull requests
watchOut: Agent features feel less integrated than Cursor

name: Cursor
bestFor: Developers who want an AI-first editor with multi-file edits
summary: A VS Code-based editor rebuilt around AI: fast tab completions, codebase-aware chat and an agent that edits across many files.
does: An AI-first code editor that predicts edits and changes many files at once
strengths: Choice of models from several vendors
watchOut: Heavy agent use costs more than the $20 sticker price

name: Claude Code
startingPrice: Included with Claude Pro (about $20/mo) and Max
bestFor: Agentic, terminal-first work on large codebases
summary: An agentic coding tool that runs in the terminal, IDE, desktop and web, reading your repo, running commands and making multi-step changes.
does: An agent that plans, edits files, runs tests and iterates until the task is done
strengths: Scriptable with hooks, commands and MCP
Included with Claude Pro and Max
watchOut: Usage limits shared with Claude chat

name: Midjourney
bestFor: Striking, art-directed imagery and mood boards
summary: The aesthetic leader for artistic and photographic images, with strong style controls, but no free plan and no public API.
does: Generates art-directed images and animates stills into short clips
strengths: Strongest sense of style and composition
Style references keep a look consistent

name: Ideogram
bestFor: Images with legible text: posters, logos, thumbnails
summary: An image generator that renders typography reliably, making it the go-to for social graphics, posters and logo concepts.
inputs: Text prompts with the exact words to show
does: Generates images that render typography reliably
watchOut: Artistic output a step behind Midjourney

name: Adobe Firefly
bestFor: Commercially safe images inside Photoshop and Express workflows
summary: Adobe's generative image suite, trained with commercial use in mind and built into Photoshop, with access to partner models too.
does: Generates and edits images inside Photoshop, Illustrator and Express
strengths: IP indemnity on some enterprise plans
watchOut: Adobe credit system takes some reading

name: Perplexity
bestFor: Research where you need to check every source
summary: An answer engine that cites sources inline for every claim, with model choice and deep research on its Pro plan.
does: Searches the web and writes an answer with a citation on every claim
strengths: Every sentence links to its source
Source filters for academic or social results
watchOut: Weaker for local businesses, maps and shopping

name: ChatGPT Search
bestFor: Search that turns into a follow-up conversation or a task
summary: Web search built into ChatGPT, best when a search becomes a longer conversation, a draft or a multi-step task.
does: Searches the web inside a ChatGPT conversation that can continue into work
outputs: Drafts and analysis built on the results
strengths: Search flows into writing, code and agents

name: Google AI Mode
bestFor: Everyday, local and shopping searches
summary: Google Search's conversational mode, backed by Google's index, Maps and Shopping data, free for everyone.
does: Answers conversationally using Google's index, Maps, reviews and Shopping data
strengths: Best for local, shopping and fresh news
watchOut: Can read like a summary of top results

name: Otter.ai
bestFor: Live transcription for lectures, interviews and in-person meetings
summary: A veteran transcription tool with live captions, a mobile recorder and an AI chat over your meeting history.
does: Transcribes conversations live and answers questions about them
strengths: Best for in-person and live transcription
watchOut: Free plan caps minutes and conversation length

name: Fireflies.ai
bestFor: Sales and ops teams that want notes pushed into a CRM
summary: A meeting bot with deep integrations into CRMs, project tools and Slack, plus conversation analytics for teams.
inputs: Calls on Zoom, Meet, Teams, Webex and more
does: Records meetings and routes notes into CRMs and team tools
outputs: Notes synced to CRMs and Slack
watchOut: Free plan caps storage and AI credits

name: Fathom
startingPrice: Generous free plan; paid plans available
bestFor: Individuals who want unlimited free recordings
summary: A meeting recorder with a famously generous free plan, unlimited recordings and transcripts, and clean highlights.
does: Records and transcribes calls with clean summaries and highlight clips
watchOut: Built for video calls, not in person

name: Grok
startingPrice: Free; paid plans via SuperGrok and X Premium
bestFor: Real-time takes on what is happening on X
summary: xAI's assistant, with live access to posts on X and a looser conversational style than most rivals.
does: Answers questions with live access to posts on X
watchOut: Best value only if you use X

name: Meta AI
bestFor: Quick help inside WhatsApp, Instagram and Messenger
summary: Meta's free assistant, built into WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook and Messenger as well as its own app.
does: Answers questions inside Meta's apps you already use
strengths: Already inside WhatsApp, Instagram and Messenger

name: Microsoft Copilot
bestFor: People who work in Word, Excel, Outlook and Windows
summary: Microsoft's assistant, free on the web and Windows, and built into Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook on Microsoft 365 plans.
inputs: Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook files
does: Answers and drafts inside Windows and Microsoft 365 apps
outputs: Answers on the web and Windows
strengths: Free version on web and Windows
watchOut: Best features need a Microsoft 365 plan

name: Leonardo AI
startingPrice: Free daily credits; paid plans available
bestFor: Game art, characters and consistent asset sets
summary: An image platform with fine-grained controls, trained styles and a free daily allowance, popular for game and concept art.
does: Generates images with fine-grained controls for game and concept art
watchOut: More controls to learn than simpler tools

name: Runway
bestFor: Filmmakers who want editing control over AI shots
summary: A creative video suite with text- and image-to-video models plus tools for editing, restyling and extending shots.
does: Generates and edits video shots in one production suite
strengths: Generation and editing in one place

name: Kling
startingPrice: Free daily credits; paid from about $10/mo
bestFor: Realistic motion on a budget
summary: A video generator known for realistic human motion and long clips, with a free daily credit allowance.
does: Turns prompts and images into realistic video clips
watchOut: Queues at busy times on lower tiers

name: Google Veo
startingPrice: Included with Google AI Pro (about $20/mo) and Ultra
bestFor: Clips with native sound and dialogue
summary: Google's video model, available in Gemini and Flow, that generates video together with matching sound.
does: Generates video together with matching sound and dialogue
outputs: Clips with sound effects and dialogue
strengths: Native audio saves a post-production step
watchOut: Highest limits only on the top plan

name: ElevenLabs
bestFor: The most natural voices, cloning and dubbing
summary: The leading AI voice platform: lifelike text-to-speech, voice cloning, dubbing and an API for developers.
does: Turns text into lifelike speech, clones voices and dubs video
strengths: Real free tier and cheap entry plan
watchOut: Many features and credit types to learn

name: Murf AI
startingPrice: Limited free preview; paid from about $19/mo
bestFor: Voiceovers for training videos and presentations
summary: A voiceover studio that lines narration up with slides and video, aimed at training, marketing and explainer content.
does: Produces voiceovers synced to slides and video on a timeline
strengths: Sentence-level control of pitch and pace
watchOut: Free option is only a preview
Entry plans cost more than ElevenLabs

name: WellSaid
bestFor: Enterprise teams that need consistent, brand-safe voices
summary: An enterprise voice platform focused on consistent, commercially licensed voices with team controls.
does: Produces consistent, licensed voices for enterprise narration

name: Gamma
bestFor: Turning notes or a prompt into a deck in minutes
summary: An AI presentation maker that generates decks, documents and web pages from a prompt or pasted notes.
does: Generates a designed deck, document or web page from rough input
strengths: Best first draft from the least input
watchOut: Distinctive layouts may not fit corporate templates

name: Beautiful.ai
bestFor: Teams that want consistently on-brand slides
summary: A presentation tool whose Smart Slides automatically re-layout as you edit, so decks stay tidy and on brand.
does: Lays out slides automatically with Smart Slides that adapt as you edit
strengths: Hard to make an ugly slide

name: Canva
bestFor: Design-heavy decks and social graphics in one tool
summary: Canva's design suite with AI features for presentations, documents and social posts, and a generous free plan.
does: Designs decks plus social posts, documents, video and print in one tool
strengths: Useful free plan with presentation export
